overview: This 173-page file surveys Japanese civil, army, and naval aviation in the 1930s, covering routes, airfields, subsidies, manufacturers, and flight rules. It also traces Ford Motor Company’s efforts to secure demonstration-flight permits in Japan and China, including a dispute over Japanese authority to regulate flights above the South Manchuria Railway Zone.
interest: Detailed aviation surveys and Ford permit correspondence reveal how commercial flying intersected with Japanese restrictions and contested jurisdiction in Manchuria.
